title: Resume browser chips — round 3: the phone filter panel, redone

steps.path: On a phone-width window → tap the filter button
steps.headline: The phone filter panel now holds the same three chips as the desktop row: two dropdowns and the sort chip.
steps.changed: The chip rows for Project and Tags and the two-way Order switch are gone. In their place are the desktop Projects and Tags dropdown chips and the Most recent sort chip, wrapping onto a second line when they need to.
steps.notice: The controls behave exactly as they do on desktop: Projects and Tags open their menus, Most recent flips with one tap. Clear at the top empties both filters.
steps.risk: The panel is smaller than round 2's, so the list under it shows through sooner.

steps.path: On a phone-width window → filter button → Projects
steps.headline: A dropdown opened inside the phone panel is the same menu as on desktop, and the panel stays open behind it.
steps.changed: Tapping Projects or Tags inside the panel opens the menu under that chip; picking rows keeps both the menu and the panel open, and a tap outside closes them together.
steps.notice: Tick several projects, then tap Tags without anything closing on you. A long project list scrolls inside its menu.

steps.path: Chips row → Most recent, after one tap
steps.headline: The sort chip carries the sort bars you picked, and the bars turn narrow-to-wide for oldest first.
steps.changed: Three bars with a down arrow replace the two-way arrows: wide-to-narrow for newest first, narrow-to-wide for oldest first.
steps.notice: Nothing else on the row changed.
